source.title: On the open problems connected to the results of Lazer and Solimini

accepted.question_text: Let omega > 0. Let g:(0,+infinity)->(0,+infinity) be continuous with g(x)->+infinity as x->0+ and g(x)->0 as x->+infinity. Let h be an omega-periodic integrable real-valued function, and consider positive omega-periodic Caratheodory solutions u in AC^1_omega((0,+infinity)) of u''(t)+g(u(t))=h(t) for almost every real t. The Lazer-Solimini existence criterion for essentially bounded h says that, when h is omega-periodic and essentially bounded, such a positive solution exists if and only if the mean value h_bar=(1/omega) integral_0^omega h(s) ds is positive. Does the same existence criterion remain valid when the essential-boundedness assumption on h is removed and h is only integrable?

evidence.quote: Does Theorem 1.1 remain still valid if the condition (1.4) is violated?
Despite of all expectations, the answer is negative.
